application_guidance.input_pattern: Bounded monotone VI with an exact compatible prox and fresh uniform bias/second-moment SO estimates.

sensitive_conditions: Both updates use the same previous corrector as prox base.
The second oracle sample is fresh relative to the history containing wτ.
The output is the predictor average; the initialization is the distance-generator center.
The second moment is around F(z), not merely around EΞ(z,ζ).
The bound concerns E[max_u gap], not max_u E[gap].

complexity_scope.guarantee: Expectation only; nonzero bias μ is allowed. No tail, Nash functional-gap, last-iterate or optimality claim is included.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: All coefficients in the bound are explicit. Geometry enters through Ω; SO and prox costs are not identified.
complexity_scope.oracle: Two sequential fresh SO calls per iteration satisfying uniform Assumption I; exact prox access is a separate capability.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Arithmetic average of predictor points wτ; expected weak gap E[max_{u∈Z}<F(u),z_hat_t-u>].
complexity_scope.regime: All finite nonnegative L,M,μ,σ and integer t≥1, with fixed γ>0 satisfying √3 Lγ≤1.
complexity_scope.resource: 2t SO calls and 2t exact prox minimizations; initialization requires computing zc, and output requires accumulation and averaging. No arithmetic complexity for those operations is asserted.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Performance upper bound for the explicitly defined fresh-sample, constant-step SMP Algorithm; no unrestricted algorithm class or lower bound is covered.

content.intended_use: An explicit upper bound on expected weak gap of the selected SMP output.

proofs.locator: PDF pp.19–23 §5.1 Theorem 2 and equations (64)–(82); PDF p.24 §5.2 through (86) and conclusion of part (i)
map: Source §5.1: the prox optimality inequality (68) gives Lemma 3, equations (69)–(70). Corollary 2, equations (73)–(75), controls an auxiliary prox sequence. Lemma 4, equations (76)–(77), supplies the two-prox estimate. These are internal source dependencies, not external lead records.

Define Δτ=F(wτ)-F_hat(wτ), ε_z=||F_hat(z)-F(z)||_* and auxiliary y0=r0, yτ=P_{y_{τ-1}}(γτΔτ), equation (64). Equations (78)–(79) combine the operator condition and step cap with Lemma 4, telescope V, and split the error term using y_{τ-1}.

Corollary 2 bounds the remaining auxiliary error sum; equations (67) and (80) give a certificate valid for all u∈Z. Monotonicity and the weighted predictor average yield Theorem 2's general VI gap bound (66), on pp.22–23. The Nash specialization is not used here.
For r0=zc and constant γ, pp.23–24 equations (81)–(82) give Err_vi(z_hat_t)≤Γ(t)/(tγ), with Γ(t)≤Ω²+(7γ²/2)Στ[M²+ε²_{r_{τ-1}}+ε²_{wτ}]+γΣτ<Δτ,wτ-y_{τ-1}>.

The pre-corrector history Fτ contains ζ1,…,ζ_{2τ-1}; wτ and y_{τ-1} are measurable with respect to it. Freshness and Assumption I yield conditional second moments ≤σ² and ||E[Δτ|Fτ]||_*≤μ, equation (83). Equation (85) bounds the expected quadratic sum by (7γ²t/2)(M²+2σ²).

By (18), all trajectory and auxiliary points lie within radius Ω of zc. Equation (86) bounds each conditional cross-term expectation by μ||wτ-y_{τ-1}||≤2μΩ. Substitution into (81)–(82), followed by division by tγ, gives (23), as concluded by the source on p.24.

proofs.reading_coverage: Page-labelled text and original-page images for relevant portions of pp.19–24: Theorem 2 setup, prox lemmas and general VI certificate, then Theorem 1(i) expectation argument through (86).

assumptions: For all z,z'∈Z°, <ω'(z)-ω'(z'),z-z'>≥||z-z'||²; the source setup and exact prox minimizations above are used.

Ξ:Z×R^N→E is Borel. At each call ζ_i is a fresh draw from an iid sequence, independent of the preceding history. Thus the corrector's random sample is fresh even though its query wτ depends on the predictor response.
Uniformly for every z∈Z, ||E[Ξ(z,ζ_i)-F(z)]||_*≤μ and E||Ξ(z,ζ_i)-F(z)||_*²≤σ² (Assumption I). Assumption II is not required.
The horizon t and constant stepsize γ are fixed in advance; r0=zc and √3 Lγ≤1.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let E be finite-dimensional Euclidean with arbitrary norm ||·|| and dual ||·||_*. Let Z⊂E be nonempty compact convex and F:Z→E bounded. Define Err_vi(z)=max_{u∈Z}<F(u),z-u>. Let ω:Z→R be continuous convex, with Z°={z∈Z:∂ω(z)≠∅} and a continuous subgradient selection ω' on Z°. Define V(z,u)=ω(u)-ω(z)-<ω'(z),u-z>, zc=argmin_Z ω, Θ(z)=max_{u∈Z}V(z,u), Ω=√(2Θ(zc)), and P_z(ξ)=argmin_{u∈Z}{V(z,u)+<ξ,u>}∈Z°. Starting from r0=zc, for τ=1,…,t set aτ=Ξ(r_{τ-1},ζ_{2τ-1}), wτ=P_{r_{τ-1}}(γaτ), bτ=Ξ(wτ,ζ_{2τ}), rτ=P_{r_{τ-1}}(γbτ), and z_hat_t=t^{-1}Σwτ.
statement.parameter_domains: L,M,μ,σ are finite nonnegative real numbers; t∈{1,2,…}; γ>0 with √3 Lγ≤1. The latter condition gives no finite upper cap when L=0. Ω is determined by the chosen distance generator and Z.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every problem, setup and SO satisfying these assumptions, every positive integer t and every positive constant γ satisfying the stated step condition, the conclusion holds with expectation over the 2t sequential fresh oracle samples. The maximum over u defining Err_vi is inside the expectation.
